title: DevX Embedded Sandbox: Chaos & Metrics Lab Runbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook describes the DevX Embedded Sandbox Chaos & Metrics Lab: a reproducible environment and process for exercising SDK + client integration failure modes, measuring telemetry signal quality, and producing canonical fixes for top support issues. The Lab is intended for developer-experience engineers, on-call support, and SDK maintainers.

Goals
- Provide a low-friction sandbox that mirrors production request/response shapes and token budgets.
- Enable controlled failure injection (network/TLS/latency/partial responses) and workload perturbation (concurrency spikes, bursty prompts).
- Validate telemetry cohorts, golden traces, and alert thresholds before shipping SDK changes.
- Produce actionable canonical fixes and reproducible tickets for product/support teams.

Scope and Non-Scope
- Included: JS/TS and Python SDKs, local telemetry agent, replay harness, failure-injector, cost/latency profiling hooks.
- Excluded: full GPU runtime performance testing (use eng-serving-runtime benchmarking suites), customer-specific private deployment configurations unless a dedicated private-lab exists.

Architecture (high level)
- Sandbox controller: CLI + lightweight web UI that orchestrates runs and retains artifacts.
- Local telemetry agent: captures in-process SDK events, token counts, latencies, and sampling flags; exposes a replayable trace archive (.trace.json).
- Failure-injector: configurable middleware that can simulate: timeouts, truncated streams, 502/503 responses, slow TLS handshakes, and intermittent connection drops.
- Golden runner: a scenario harness that executes prompt bundles and compares outputs/metrics against goldens.

Key components and ownership
- devx-sandbox (service template): Owner: DevX SDK team (Maya Chen). Contains docker-compose for the sandbox stack.
- telemetry-agent (library): Owner: Observability team (Carlos Ruiz). Emits schema v2 events and provides trace archival.
- injector (module): Owner: Reliability & Platform (Anita Patel). Implements failure primitives and blast-radius controls.

SLOs and success criteria for lab runs
- Turnaround: sandbox should be deployable locally in < 5 minutes (cold start).
- Trace quality: >95% of SDK calls include correlation_id and token_count fields.
- Determinism: golden-run comparisons should be reproducible in 9/10 consecutive runs; tolerances configured per scenario.
- Triage signal: failing scenario must produce at least one of the following: error-level trace, latency spike > 2x baseline, or token-count deviation > 10%.

Quickstart: Local sandbox (3-minute developer path)
1) Prereqs: Docker (20.10+), Node 18+/Python 3.10+, git.
2) Clone repo and bring up stack:
   git clone git@repo.redwood.ai:devx/devx-sandbox.git
   cd devx-sandbox
   ./bin/start-local.sh --profile default
3) Run a smoke scenario against the bundled SDK sample (Node):
   cd examples/node-streaming
   npm install
   SDK_SANDBOX_URL=http://localhost:8080 node run-smoke.js
4) Capture a trace and export golden:
   ./bin/collect-trace.sh --scenario=smoke --out=goldens/smoke.trace.json

Failure-injection matrix (example)
| Scenario | Failure type | Expected metric change | Blast radius | Runbook step on failure |
| Network flaps during streaming | intermittent connection reset | stream-error rate +50% | low (1 container) | increase retry-backoff and verify stream-idempotency |
| Truncated response mid-stream | server closes connection after N tokens | partial-response traces, user-visible truncation | medium | enable fallback-to-sync and replay last-segment |
| Elevated latency for model init | 5–10s slow path on cold start | startup p95 > SLA (2s) | high | enable prewarm policy and adjust client connect timeout |

Experiment templates and YAML examples
- Scenario definition (yaml):
  name: streaming-truncate-check
  description: Validate client handles truncated streams and replays last 2KB of prompt
  failure_injection:
    - type: truncate_stream
      after_tokens: 128
      probability: 0.5
  metrics_expectation:
    latency_p95_ms: 1200
    stream_error_rate_percent: 10

- Local CLI run (example):
  ./bin/run-scenario --scenario=streaming-truncate-check --iterations=50 --telemetry=sampled

Telemetry: sampling, cohorts, golden traces
- Sampling policy: default sample-rate = 1/10 for non-failing runs; sample all failing runs and any run marked smoke.
- Cohorts: SDK-language (js/python), runtime-mode (streaming/sync), route (generation/embeddings). Label traces with these fields for cohort-based alerting.
- Golden traces: store in /goldens with CI gating. Golden artifacts include: request bundle (.jsonl), trace (.trace.json), response-checksum (.sha256).

CI integration and gating
- Add a CI job "devx/telemetry-golden-check" that:
  1) Boots a headless sandbox via docker-compose with deterministic fixtures.
  2) Runs golden scenarios and compares trace diffs with tolerant thresholds.
  3) Fails the pipeline if regressions exceed configured thresholds (latency, token_count, error_rate).

Canonical fix playbook (when a lab run surfaces a reproducible issue)
1) Triage: assign to SDK owner and attach the trace artifact + failing request bundle.
2) Root cause hypotheses (2h): run targeted experiments (increase sampling, run with debug logs, compare code branches).
3) Patch + unit tests: add behavioral unit test in sdk-integration-suite that replicates the trimming/retry case.
4) CI goldens: update golden only if behavior change is intentional; otherwise produce a rollback patch for the SDK change that introduced the regression.
5) Postmortem artifact: short-form writeup (owner, cause, fix, release version, rollback window) and link to the ticket.

Top support issues mapped to lab scenarios
- "Client sees truncated streamed reply" -> scenario: streaming-truncate-check -> fix: strengthen streaming checksum and idempotent resume.
- "High token counts on short prompts" -> scenario: tokenizer-leak-sim -> fix: isolate and patch double-encode path.
- "Unexpected 502s during bursts" -> scenario: concurrency-burst-502 -> fix: client-side concurrency slotting and exponential jitter.

Safety and blast-radius controls
- All failure injections default to "local" network namespace.
- When running in shared CI pool, set BLAST_RADIUS=ci-small and require two approvers before enabling medium/high blast radius.
- Audit: injector logs are archived alongside trace artifacts for 30 days (configurable).

Operational checklist (pre-run)
- Verify telemetry-agent version matches the golden schema v2.
- Confirm golden artifacts checksum and CI env variables.
- Notify on-call Slack channel #devx-labs with run id and expected duration.

How to onboard a new SDK or scenario
1) Create scenario bundle in devx-scenarios/ with request samples, expected checksums, and a scenario.yaml.
2) Add a runner in examples/ that demonstrates minimal usage pattern and exposes a smoke endpoint.
3) Request reviewer from Observability and Reliability via the "lab-onboard" GitHub action.

Troubleshooting tips
- If sandbox fails to start: run ./bin/start-local.sh --debug and inspect logs in ./logs. Typical causes: port conflicts, old docker images, or Compose version mismatch.
- If traces lack correlation_id: bump telemetry-agent to >= v2.1.0 and re-run with --full-trace.

Appendix: Example Node snippet (stream resume)
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ baseUrl: process.env.SDK_SANDBOX_URL, timeoutMs: 120000 });
async function resumeStream(sessionId) {
  try {
    const res = await client.streamResume({ sessionId });
    res.on('data', (chunk) => console.log(chunk.text));
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('resume failed', err);
    // canonical fallback: sync fetch last chunk then restart streaming
  }
}
